text:
cam: alert - SEV2: multiple nodes in gpu-pool-3 showing repeated OOM / CUDA errors from paged-attn allocator. Started ~1765432199, seen node flaps and a couple container restarts. Prom alerts: paged_kv_fragmentation_increase, allocator_oom_rate > 0.5/min. Investigating.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED - #sev2-kv-paged-gremlin (priority p0) — Assigned to eng-oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paged-kv-oom

maria: seeing similar on s-03 and s-07. CUDA driver shows device-side allocation failures in logs: `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` across many short-lived containers. Also slab bitmap shows fragmentation spike.

cam: any customer-facing errors? Ops dashboard shows increase in 5xx for model-serving route /v1/generate on hosted region eu-west-1. Spike aligns with node flaps 1765432205..1765432210.

ops-shift: flagged two paying customers on enterprise tier reporting request timeouts, support ticket linked: INC-4721. Low percent (~0.8%) of overall requests but important customers. Triage priority: mitigate to restore SLA.

derek: quick mitigation proposal: 1) Reduce default batch size for paged-attn models to 1 on at-risk nodes via runtime flag `--batch-max=1` to lower transient allocation pressure 2) Enable soft-evict for KV pages: `runtimectl set kv-evict soft` 3) Route new traffic away from nodes with fragmentation > 70% by temporary routing policy.

sukanya: agree. Also advise enabling fallback to non-paged model variant (unpaged or smaller kv cache) for hosted tier while we stabilize. Add config: `fallback_policy: variant:nonpaged, threshold:alloc_fail_rate>0.2`

cam: executing step 3 now — adding node label `kv-suspect=true` and updating routing rule to avoid those nodes. Will post k8s commands.

cam: run: ```
kubectl label node s-03 kv-suspect=true --overwrite
kubectl label node s-07 kv-suspect=true --overwrite
# update routing config
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"avoid_nodes":"kv-suspect"}' https://runtime-admin.internal/routing/policy
```

maria: performing quick runtime probe to dump allocator metrics: ```
runtime-admin exec --node s-03 --bin allocator-inspect --slab-stats
# returns: total_pages=128K, frag_ratio=0.72, resident_alloc=91%
```

derek: frag_ratio 0.72 is bad. Start gradual drain of s-03 and s-07 to evict warm KV entries and let compaction run. Use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data s-03` after routing cutover.

cam: initiating drain on s-07 first (lower qps). Will coordinate rolling restarts to avoid simultaneous capacity loss.

oncall-bot: NOTE: Rolling restart in progress for s-07 at 1765432209.

ops-shift: customer impact update: support notified both affected customers of degraded latency/5xx, ETA for next update 30m. Telemetry link: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/dashboards/kv-frag?since=1h

sukanya: additional mitigation: drop background compaction threshold to be more aggressive: `runtimectl set compaction.threshold 0.5` — this will increase CPU but should reduce fragmentation. Schedule to revert once stable.

maria: other nodes show slow-creep fragmentation, likely due to small allocation pattern regression in latest allocator changes (deployed in canary earlier this week). Suggest pinning canary back to previous allocator build on affected capacity pool.

derek: agree — start canary rollback on gpu-pool-3. How long will we need the fallback? Estimate 45-60 minutes for drains + compaction to reduce frag.

cam: rollback command queued: `deployctl rollback --service allocator --to-revision r2024-11-10 --pool gpu-pool-3` — kicked off at 1765432212. Monitoring.

maria: post-rollback logs show allocation failures dropping on s-07 after restart. s-03 still showing residual fragmentation; compaction in progress and OOMs have stopped for new containers.

ops-shift: support updated customers at 1765432215: they acknowledged, asked for RCA timeline. We committed to follow-up with a detailed incident timeline in 24h.

derek: next steps checklist in thread: - monitor frag_ratio and allocator_oom_rate for 2x SLO windows - keep routing avoidance for nodes with frag>0.6 - hold canary until we validate perf and compaction stabilizes - create hotfix to tighten page allocation path (engineering ticket: ENG-9732)

cam: assigning ENG-9732 and ENG-9733 (postmortem/telemetry gaps). If we see re-flare, escalate to infra-sre for potential kernel-level driver investigation.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE at 1765432218 — mitigation partially successful, routing avoids flagged nodes, rollback completed for allocator canary, no new OOMs reported in last 30s. Keep watch for 1h.

maria: adding a brief how-to to ops runbook for future rapid soft-evict and fallback route: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paged-kv-oom#quick-mitigation

cam: thanks team. I'll open the postmortem draft and link telemetry + customer timeline. Will reconvene in 1h unless re-alerts. :thumbsup:
